name: QuEChERS
nav: Extraction salts and tubes for multi-residue methods
metaTitle: QuEChERS Extraction Salts and Tubes in India | Acurris Analytical
metaDesc: Original, AOAC 2007.01 and EN 15662 QuEChERS salt formulations in pouches or tubes, stocked in India. Request a quote or an evaluation pack.
summary: QuEChERS salts drive the extraction and partitioning step in multi-residue pesticide and contaminant methods. We supply the three standard formulations in pre-weighed pouches and centrifuge tubes, so your analysts stop weighing salts by hand.

types.name: Original (unbuffered)
types.detail: 4 g magnesium sulfate, 1 g sodium chloride, for a 10 g sample
types.use: General fruit, vegetable and cereal work where pH-sensitive analytes are not a concern

types.name: AOAC 2007.01 (acetate buffered)
types.detail: 6 g magnesium sulfate, 1.5 g sodium acetate, for a 15 g sample
types.use: Labs running the AOAC official method, and pH-sensitive pesticides

types.name: EN 15662 (citrate buffered)
types.detail: 4 g magnesium sulfate, 1 g sodium chloride, 1 g trisodium citrate dihydrate, 0.5 g disodium hydrogen citrate sesquihydrate, for a 10 g sample
types.use: Labs accredited to the European standard method

types.name: Pouches or tubes
types.detail: Pre-weighed pouches to add to your own tubes, or 50 mL centrifuge tubes with salts already inside
types.use: Pouches suit labs with existing tube stock. Pre-filled tubes save a transfer step

methodFit: Start from the method your lab is accredited for. If your NABL scope lists AOAC 2007.01, use acetate salts. If it lists EN 15662, use citrate salts. Switching formulation changes recoveries for some analytes and usually means revalidating.

Dry commodities such as cereals, pulses, spices and tea need water added before extraction, because the salts need an aqueous phase to partition against. Most labs add water to bring a reduced sample weight up to around 80 percent water content, then follow the method as written.

Extraction is half the job. Raw extracts from fatty, pigmented or sugary matrices carry co-extractives that foul GC liners and suppress LC-MS signal, so most methods follow QuEChERS with a dSPE cleanup step.

faq.q: Which QuEChERS formulation should I use?
faq.a: Use the one your validated method specifies. If you are setting up a new method, the buffered versions give more consistent recoveries for pH-sensitive pesticides. Tell us your analyte list and matrix and we will suggest a starting point.

faq.q: Should I buy pouches or pre-filled tubes?
faq.a: Pre-filled tubes remove one handling step and suit high sample volumes. Pouches cost less per test if you already stock 50 mL centrifuge tubes.

faq.q: Can you match the salts I use now?
faq.a: Send us the formulation and fill weights from your current method or supplier. We will confirm whether we can match them before you order.

faq.q: Do you supply the cleanup step too?
faq.a: Yes. Our dSPE tubes pair with each QuEChERS formulation. See the dSPE page or ask for both in one quote.

faq.q: Can I test before I commit to a volume order?
faq.a: Yes. Request a paid evaluation pack after you send a quote request. The pack cost is credited against your first order.

name: Mycotoxins
nav: Aflatoxins, ochratoxin A, DON, zearalenone, fumonisins
metaTitle: Mycotoxin Rapid Test Kits in India: Aflatoxin, DON, OTA | Acurris Analytical
metaDesc: Rapid screening kits for aflatoxin B1, total aflatoxins, ochratoxin A, DON, zearalenone and fumonisins in grain, oilseeds and feed. Stocked in India.
summary: Rapid mycotoxin kits let you screen grain, oilseeds and feed ingredients at intake, before a contaminated lot enters storage or production. We supply kits for the five toxin groups that matter most in Indian commodities.

types.name: Aflatoxin B1 and total aflatoxins
types.use: Maize, groundnut, rice, spices, oilseed cake, compound feed

typesNote: Kit format (strip or microplate), range and extraction solvent vary by toxin. Your quote states them for each kit.
methodFit: Sampling causes most of the error in mycotoxin results. Toxins cluster in a few kernels, so a small grab sample from one bag can miss a contaminated lot or condemn a clean one. Take many small increments across the lot, combine them, grind the whole aggregate, and test a subsample of the ground material.

Decide whether you need a yes or no answer at a limit, or a number. Qualitative kits suit intake decisions against a single acceptance limit. Semi-quantitative and quantitative kits suit buyers who grade lots or price by contamination level.

Rapid kits screen. They do not replace confirmatory methods such as HPLC with fluorescence detection or LC-MS/MS. Send presumptive positives and results near your limit to a confirming lab, and keep both results on file.

faq.q: Do rapid mycotoxin kits replace HPLC?
faq.a: No. Use rapid kits to screen many lots fast and cheaply, and confirm positives or borderline results by HPLC or LC-MS/MS.

faq.q: How much sample should I collect?
faq.a: Collect as many increments as practical across the whole lot and grind the full aggregate before you subsample. Our technical team can help you set a sampling plan for your commodity and lot size.

faq.q: Can I test several toxins from one extract?
faq.a: Some kit combinations share an extraction solvent and some do not. Tell us which toxins you test together and we will confirm in the quote.

faq.q: Do the kits work for spices and oilcakes?
faq.a: Spices, oilcakes and compound feed carry pigments and fats that can interfere with rapid tests. Tell us your matrix and we will confirm suitability before you order.

faq.q: Can I test before I commit to a volume order?
faq.a: Yes. Request a paid evaluation pack after you send a quote request. The pack cost is credited against your first order.

name: Antibiotic residues
h1: Antibiotic and veterinary drug residue test kits
metaTitle: Antibiotic Residue Test Kits for Milk in India | Acurris Analytical
metaDesc: Rapid screening kits for beta-lactam, tetracycline, sulfonamide, fluoroquinolone and macrolide residues in milk, honey, meat and shrimp. Stocked in India.
summary: Antibiotic residue kits give a fast accept or reject decision on raw milk at collection and on other animal-origin foods before processing or export. We supply kits across the main veterinary drug classes.

types.name: Other veterinary drugs
types.use: Tell us the analyte and matrix

typesNote: Single-class and combined tests are available for some classes. Your quote states format, detection levels and read time for each kit.
methodFit: At milk collection, speed and simplicity decide whether a test gets used on every tanker. Combined beta-lactam and tetracycline tests cover the drugs most often found in milk in one run, and most collection points start there.

Incubation temperature and read time matter more than operators expect. Run tests in a calibrated incubator, read inside the stated window, and keep samples cold until testing. Most false results trace back to one of these three steps.

Know which limits your buyer applies. Domestic supply follows FSSAI limits, and export buyers often apply their own. Pick kits whose detection levels sit at or below the strictest limit you face, and confirm positives by LC-MS/MS.

faq.q: Which test should a milk collection point start with?
faq.a: Most start with a combined beta-lactam and tetracycline test, then add other classes based on local veterinary drug use and buyer requirements.

faq.q: Do I need an incubator?
faq.a: Most receptor and lateral flow tests for milk need a dry-block incubator at a fixed temperature. Tell us what equipment you have and we will match kits to it.

faq.q: Can these kits be used for shrimp or honey?
faq.a: Some drug classes have kits for shrimp, honey and meat. These matrices need different sample preparation from milk. Tell us your matrix and we will confirm.

faq.q: What happens when a sample tests positive?
faq.a: Treat it as presumptive. Hold the lot, retest, and send the sample to a lab for confirmation by LC-MS/MS before you reject or report it.

faq.a: Yes. Request a paid evaluation pack after you send a quote request. The pack cost is credited against your first order.

nav: Milk adulterants, synthetic milk, non-permitted colors

metaTitle: Milk Adulteration Test Kits in India: Urea, Starch, Detergent | Acurris Analytical
metaDesc: Rapid kits to screen milk for synthetic milk, urea, starch and detergent, and foods for non-permitted colors. For collection centers, dairy plants and labs.
summary: Adulteration kits let collection staff and plant QA screen milk and other foods on the spot, with color-change reads and no instruments. We supply kits for the adulterants most often found in Indian milk and foods.

types.name: Synthetic milk
types.use: Raw milk at collection and intake

types.name: Other adulterants
types.use: Tell us the adulterant and matrix

typesNote: Your quote states the read method, detection level and tests per kit for each item.
methodFit: Most adulteration tests read as a color change. Read every test under the same light, against the same reference card, and inside the stated time. Daylight through a window gives different reads in the morning and evening.
Run a panel, not a single test. Adulterated milk usually carries more than one additive, because each one masks a different quality check. A panel at intake catches what one test misses.
Record every result against the supplier, date and quantity. Your records turn a one-off rejection into a pattern you can act on with the supplier.

faq.q: Who can run these tests?
faq.a: Collection center staff can run them after a short demonstration. No lab instruments are needed for most tests. Our technical team can train your staff by video call.

faq.q: How many tests should we run at intake?
faq.a: Most dairies run a panel covering urea, starch, detergent and synthetic milk at intake, then add tests based on what they find locally.

faq.q: Do positive results need confirmation?
faq.a: Yes. Treat a positive as presumptive, hold the milk, and confirm in a lab before you reject or report it.

faq.q: Do you have kits for spices and sweets?
faq.a: Yes, for non-permitted colors. Tell us the product and the colors you are checking for.

faq.q: Can I test before I commit to a volume order?
faq.a: Yes. Request a paid evaluation pack after you send a quote request. The pack cost is credited against your first order.
